description: Baseline: set up an out-of-Unity compile check (Unity Editor is open, so batchmode and test runs are impossible) and confirm the current runtime and test sources compile with 0 errors before any change.
steps: Read context.json build_command. Create an .rsp file in %TEMP% (not in the project) that compiles all .cs under Assets/Scripts excluding Tests into a library, referencing Unity managed DLLs, netstandard.dll, and Library/ScriptAssemblies/Unity.XR.Interaction.Toolkit.dll and Unity.XR.CoreUtils.dll.

Run csc with the Unity bundled dotnet.exe and record the result (0 errors expected). Also compile the test sources (Assets/Scripts/Tests/**) against the runtime output plus UnityEngine.TestRunner.dll and nunit.framework.dll (locate them under Library/ScriptAssemblies or the Unity Editor folder); if the test references cannot be found, record that and continue.
Save the working compile command as a PowerShell script outside the project (e.g. %TEMP%\compile_check.ps1) and note its path in this feature's findings so later features can rerun it.

Read Assets/Scripts/Cooking/Pan.cs, PanSnap.cs, Assets/Scripts/Tests/PlayMode/PanTests.cs and PanSnapTests.cs and note in findings every place that depends on the held object being kinematic or on XRGrabInteractable movement type, since FEAT-002 changes how held objects move.
acceptance_criteria: The csc runtime compile completes with 0 errors
Findings list the compile script path and any kinematic or movement-type dependencies found in Pan.cs, PanSnap.cs and the PlayMode tests
verification: Run the saved compile script and confirm 0 errors
findings:

Warnings are suppressed (-warn:0). Other shell notes: shell writes to the project folder and to the task .json are denied (use fs_write/str_replace); fs_write into the project works.

KINEMATIC / MOVEMENT-TYPE DEPENDENCIES (for FEAT-002):
- Pan.cs: CanStick() rejects items whose Rigidbody isKinematic (itemBody.isKinematic => false) and items whose XRBaseInteractable isSelected. So a held item (kinematic under Instantaneous mode) is never stuck. If FEAT-002 keeps held bodies non-kinematic (e.g. velocity tracking) the isSelected check still blocks sticking while held. Pan.cs sticks via FixedJoint to the pan Rigidbody (connectedBody = Body), needs the pan Rigidbody non-kinematic only if the pan itself must be pushed by the joint; the joint works with a kinematic or dynamic connected body. ReleaseInvalid() detaches stuck items when interactable.isSelected becomes true; TryStick listens to selectEntered to Detach. Pan.cs never writes isKinematic and never reads the pan's own isKinematic. FixedUpdate runs OverlapBoxNonAlloc on the disabled Contents/HeatSensor BoxColliders with QueryTriggerInteraction.Collide (so any new trigger colliders overlapping those boxes, e.g. a held-object proximity trigger, would be seen by the heat sensor only if they have a BurnerZone component, and by Contents only if they have a Cookable parent; new colliders must not carry Cookable/BurnerZone).
- PanSnap.cs: line 'if (m_ReleasedFor < m_SettleDelay || Body.isKinematic) return;' skips snapping while the pan body is kinematic; FixedUpdate resets state (ResetState) whenever m_Interactable.isSelected, so snapping is cancelled while grabbed. It moves the pan with Body.MovePosition/MoveRotation and zeroes linearVelocity/angularVelocity in Glide(), which assumes a non-kinematic body (setting velocity on a kinematic body logs a warning in some Unity versions). Class doc says it does not touch isKinematic so XRGrabInteractable cannot undo it. FindSurfaceHeight() raycasts down and ignores hits whose hit.rigidbody is non-kinematic ('Free rigidbodies (this pan, food, the knife) are not a surface'): if FEAT-002 makes other objects kinematic permanently, they would be treated as surface by this raycast, so any scripts must restore isKinematic=false after release. Timing: m_ReleasedFor is reset to 0 in ResetState while selected and counts up after release; throw velocity (ThrowOnDetach) is applied by XRGrabInteractable on selectExited, and IsCalm() requires linear speed <= 1.5 m/s, angular <= 6 rad/s, tilt <= 40 degrees after the 0.1 s settle delay. If FEAT-002 changes how velocity is applied on release, check these thresholds.
- PanTests.cs (PlayMode): the test pan Rigidbody is isKinematic = true (moved by the test with MovePosition/MoveRotation) and the Pan component is configured through Pan.Configure(contents, sensor). Steak test objects are plain spheres with Rigidbody useGravity=false (non kinematic) and no XRBaseInteractable. Tests depend on: steaks sticking only when non-kinematic and slow (<= 0.35 m/s relative), the FixedJoint being added on the steak, Detach() removing it after one frame, heat only from BurnerZone triggers overlapped by the HeatSensor box. No XR or movement-type use in these tests. Any new component added to Pan or to Cookable objects must tolerate being created without XR components and a kinematic pan body.
- PanSnapTests.cs (PlayMode): the test pan is a non-kinematic Rigidbody (useGravity true by default, or false) with a BoxCollider and a PanSnap; there is no XRGrabInteractable so m_Interactable is null (PanSnap handles null). Tests use a static cube as the surface and BurnerZone objects created with AddComponent<BurnerZone>(). They require that: a free pan falls and snaps within 45 fixed steps (0.9 s at 0.02 s), the pan is NOT snapped when speed is 4 m/s or tilt 60 degrees, the nearest burner wins, the surface raycast ignores dynamic bodies, and a pan teleported away (Rigidbody.position set) forgets the burner. A new runtime script that is attached only in the scene/prefab (FEAT-002) will not affect these tests as long as it is not added to the test objects. Neither test file references XRGrabInteractable, MovementType or selectEntered.
- XRGrabInteractable config relevant to FEAT-002: Pan.prefab uses MovementType 2 (Instantaneous), ThrowOnDetach 1, Rigidbody CollisionDetection 2 (ContinuousDynamic), Interpolate 1. In Instantaneous mode XRGrabInteractable sets isKinematic = true while held and restores the original value on drop (it caches it), which is why PanSnap/Pan avoid touching isKinematic.
